subject: Retention question: classification of interaction elements for deletion
messages:
From: Sara Lang <sara.lang@brightbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@brightbank.com
Date: Thu, 13 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying what BrightBank needs re: deletion proof and "kept" elements

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the call earlier. To keep procurement moving, our InfoSec and Legal teams need a concise statement about which interaction elements Redwood treats as persistent by default vs ephemeral (for the hosted API). In particular:

- When a customer uses the chat API, do the raw customer requests (user prompts) count as "stored logs" or are they treated as ephemeral streaming artifacts?
- For model completions / answers, are final outputs stored by default? If so, for how long and where (region/residency)?
- What about intermediate streamed fragments and KV-cache entries — are they ever persisted beyond the request lifecycle?

We also need an explanation of the deletion path: if BrightBank requests erasure of a specific session or user inputs, what evidence will you provide, and how long until tombstones/indices are removed?

I've attached a spreadsheet with the specific rows our audit team expects you to fill (brightbank-retention-qa.xlsx). Can you reply with the short answers we can include in our risk assessment? If you prefer, a one-page summary and an architecture diagram also works.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our deadline is end of day Friday.

Best,
Sara
Sara Lang
Security Program Manager, BrightBank

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lang <sara.lang@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Jul 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying what BrightBank needs re: deletion proof and "kept" elements

Sara — thanks for the clear list, and for attaching the sheet. Quick top-line answers below; I also kicked this to Legal and Product to capture edge cases and evidence steps.

- Customer requests (user prompts): by default, prompts are captured as part of the request record in the hosted product for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. They are considered "stored" in the telemetry/interaction store. We provide options to opt-out or request automatic purge on a per-account basis; for Dedicated/Private customers prompts can be configured to be non-persistent.

- Final outputs (model completions): default behavior is to retain final completions for a limited retention window used for analytics and quality regressions. The default retention window for hosted API is 45 days unless a customer opts into longer retention (e.g., for billing analytics). Residency matches the customer's region selection; EU customers' retained artifacts reside in EU regions.

- Streamed fragments & KV cache: these are transient by design. Streaming buffers and KV cache artifacts are not persisted to long-term storage as artifacts tied to customer records; they are ephemeral within inference runtime and only materialize in persistent stores if explicitly captured by the customer or by debugging/tracing that the customer has enabled.

- Deletion path & evidence: for hosted customers we provide a deletion runbook: 1) submit erasure request, 2) we mark records for deletion and purge primary stores, 3) tombstone indices are cleared within the next scheduled sweep (up to 72 hours), 4) final verification report (timestamped) provided as evidence. For Dedicated/Private we provide erasure playbooks aligned to contract terms.

I'm attaching a one-page summary and a diagram (redwood-retention-diagram.png) for the audit team; Kimberly, Karthik — can you add the technical proof points (storage paths, retention TTLs, and snapshots) to the spreadsheet?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Product Manager, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-retention-diagram.png (image), one-pager (attached to email thread)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lang <sara.lang@brightbank.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Jul 2028 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying what BrightBank needs re: deletion proof and "kept" elements

Sara / Mina — adding concrete storage and evidence items for the spreadsheet. Quick bullets that I'll paste into brightbank-retention-qa.xlsx: 

- Prompts and final completions: default hosted TTL = 45 days; storage location = customer-region blob store (S3-equivalent) under bucket redwood-telemetry-{region}. Access is limited via IAM roles; retention enforced by lifecycle policy.
- Snapshots/backups: encrypted daily snapshots kept for 7 days in a separate backup account; we do not use snapshots for analytics and they are excluded from normal erasure flows except by separate request.
- Proof-of-deletion artifacts: when we complete an erasure we provide a JSON manifest with: list of object keys removed, deletion timestamps, and the job id for the purge run. We can also provide signed acknowledgement from our KMS if required.
- Stream buffers / KV-cache: in-memory only — no persistent objects created unless debug logging explicitly enabled.

Note on opt-outs: we can configure accounts so prompts/completions are not retained at all (session-only): this is a configuration for Dedicated/Private or for hosted with an enterprise agreement. That configuration change applies prospectively and we describe the trade-offs (no analytics, limited troubleshooting).

Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lang <sara.lang@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, legal@brightbank.com
Date: Thu, 13 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying what BrightBank needs re: deletion proof and "kept" elements

Sara — looping Legal here to confirm the wording for the attestation we can provide. Summary for your audit (one-paragraph you can paste into your risk doc):

"Redwood Inference persists customer request inputs and final model outputs by default in the hosted service for a configurable retention window (default 45 days). Intermediate streamed tokens and runtime KV cache are ephemeral and not written to long-term persistent storage unless explicitly captured via debug/tracing. Customers may request erasure of stored artifacts; Redwood executes a documented purge workflow and provides a timestamped deletion manifest as evidence within 72 hours of completion for hosted customers. Residency of retained artifacts follows the customer's selected region; Dedicated and Private deployments support stricter non-persistence configurations upon contract."

If that language looks good to BrightBank Legal, we'll also fill the excel with the bucket names, TTLs, and the exact field names for the deletion manifest.

Thanks — Mina
